chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abdullah ibn al-Salt, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Islam is built upon five things: upon Salat, Zakat, Hajj, Sawm, and Wilayah.
Zurara said, So I said, And which of those is superior? He said: Wilayah is superior because it is their key, and the Wali (Guardian) is the proof upon them.
I said, Then which follows that in superiority? He said: Salat. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Salat is the pillar of your religion.

He said, I said, Then which follows it in superiority? He said: Zakat, because He paired it with it and began with Salat before it; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Zakat removes sins.
I said, And which follows it in superiority? He said: Hajj.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to undertake a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Self-sufficient above the worlds.

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: An accepted Hajj is better than twenty optional Salats. And whoever circumambulates this House with a circumambulation in which he counts its seven, and performs well his two Raka'ats, Allah will forgive him. And he said regarding the Day of Arafah and the Day of Muzdalifah what he said.

I said, So what follows it? He said: Sawm (Fasting). I said, And what is the matter that Sawm became the last of all that? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Fasting is a shield from the Fire.
He said, Then he said: Indeed, the most superior of things is that which, if it is missed by you, there is no repentance from it except that you return to it and fulfill it exactly.
Indeed, Salat, Zakat, Hajj, and Wilayah: nothing can occur in their place besides their fulfillment.

And indeed, Sawm, if it is missed by you, or you are deficient, or you travel in it, you fulfill its place with other days, and you atone for that sin with charity, and there is no Qada (making up) upon you.
And from those four, nothing else suffices you in its place.
Then he said: The peak of the matter, and its hump, and its key, and the door of the things, and the Pleasure of the Beneficent is the obedience to the Imam after knowing him.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: Whoever obeys the Messenger, he has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away, then We have not sent you as a keeper over them.

If a man were to stand in prayer his night, and fast his day, and give charity with all his wealth, and perform Hajj all his life, and did not know the Wilayah of the Wali of Allah, so he aligned with him, and all his deeds were by his guidance to him, he would not have a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His reward, nor would he be from the people of Faith.
Then he said: The good one among them, Allah will enter him into Paradise by the grace of His Mercy.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam according to Shia hadith and which is considered the most superior?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the five pillars of Islam, placing Wilayah (Guardianship) as the most superior pillar because it is the key to the others. It details the hierarchy of these pillars, emphasizing that while fasting can be made up, the other four require exact fulfillment, and ultimately, obedience to the Imam is the peak of the matter and the source of divine pleasure. In Shia scholarship, this narration is pivotal for establishing Wilayah not merely as a supplementary virtue but as the foundational 'key' (miftah) that validates the acceptance of ritual acts, distinguishing the Shia understanding of Islam's structure from other schools.
